title: 2000 Zero Zero, Party Over — Oops, Out of Time
gist: Jonah McLeod maps the AI build-out onto the 1996–2000 telecom/dot-com bubble — neoclouds as CLECs, Nvidia as Lucent/Nortel with vendor financing, token forecasts as the '100-day doubling' — while noting hyperscalers' cash flows and real AI revenue; he argues power constraints lengthen payback and that, if the pattern holds, the clock is already running, with a blockbuster Anthropic IPO completing rather than breaking the analogy.

themes.theme: AI build-out has become a utility-scale capital bet

insights.claim: A single AI rack now draws more than 100 kilowatts and a campus hundreds of megawatts, all needing large amounts of water for cooling, turning AI investment into a bet on land, water and power with utility- and railroad-like capital requirements.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: AI exposure increasingly means exposure to power, land and utility-style capex risk.
insights.quote: It had become a bet on land, water, and power, the stuff of utilities and railroads, with capital requirements to match.

insights.claim: Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta have guided to roughly $720–745 billion of 2026 capex, and spent a combined $208.7 billion in Q3 2026 alone, up 84% year over year.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler capex scale dwarfs the telecom boom, magnifying downside if returns lag.

insights.claim: In the late 1990s the Telecommunications Act of 1996 triggered a fiber gold rush by Global Crossing, Level 3, WorldCom and hundreds of CLECs, while Lucent, Nortel and Cisco sold equipment and lent customers money to buy it.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Vendor-financed demand is the historical red flag to watch in AI.
insights.locator: Viewed in the mirror of the

insights.claim: WorldCom's UUNET claim that Internet traffic doubled every 100 days, repeated even by the U.S. Commerce Department in 1998, fueled overbuilding, while Andrew Odlyzko showed the real rate was closer to doubling once a year.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Demand forecasts repeated in investor decks can be off by an order of magnitude.
insights.locator: Investor presentations repeating a claim spread

insights.claim: The telecom bust bankrupted hundreds of carriers including WorldCom and Global Crossing, sent Nortel's stock from over $100 to under a dollar, and erased about $5 trillion of Nasdaq value between March 2000 and October 2002.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Equipment vendors suffered the deepest drawdowns when financed demand collapsed.
insights.quote: Nortel’s stock fell from more than $100 to under a dollar
insights.locator: Investor presentations repeating a claim spread

insights.claim: Neoclouds are today's CLECs: upstarts building capacity with borrowed money, betting demand arrives before loan payments, many born from crypto miners with idle GPUs or power hookups (CoreWeave began by renting out Ethereum-mining GPUs).
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Leveraged neoclouds are the most fragile layer of the AI stack in a downturn.
insights.quote: These neoclouds are today’s CLECs: upstarts building capacity with borrowed money, betting that demand will arrive before the loan payments do.

insights.claim: Nvidia plays the role of Lucent and Nortel, having taken stakes in customers from CoreWeave to OpenAI and in some cases promised to buy capacity they cannot sell.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Circular vendor financing ties Nvidia's revenue quality to neocloud solvency.
insights.quote: Today’s Lucent and Nortel is Nvidia

insights.claim: Projections of exploding AI inference token demand are today's equivalent of the 100-day traffic doubling, repeated in investor decks until they sound like settled fact.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Skepticism warranted toward token-growth forecasts underpinning capex plans.
insights.quote: The 100-day doubling has become the token forecast

insights.claim: Unlike fiber laid in 1999 that still carries traffic, a GPU bought in 2024 may be outdated within a few years, so if demand stalls GPU hardware loses value faster than any fiber did.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Faster depreciation makes an AI overbuild more punishing for asset-backed lenders and neoclouds than the fiber glut.
insights.quote: A GPU bought in 2024 may be outdated within a few years

insights.claim: Today's largest AI builders are the most profitable companies on earth paying mostly from cash flow, and AI has real revenue because businesses pay for work done, unlike CLECs selling unused capacity.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler balance sheets cushion a bust better than in 2000.

insights.claim: The real question is not whether AI demand is real but whether it can grow fast enough to justify the capacity being built.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Frames the investment debate around growth rate versus capacity, not existence of demand.
insights.quote: The question is not whether AI demand is real but whether it can grow fast enough to justify the capacity being built.

insights.claim: Hyperscalers have turned to the bond market and off-balance-sheet partnerships to fund data centers, and neoclouds carry CLEC-like debt loads, so the cash-flow cushion is getting thinner one bond deal at a time.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Rising AI-related debt issuance is a leading indicator of bubble risk.
insights.quote: The cash-flow cushion is getting thinner, one bond deal at a time.

insights.claim: Model makers' revenue is growing fast but breakeven keeps receding: Anthropic raised its 2026 revenue forecast yet pushed back its expected cash-flow-positive date, as each new model costs more to train and price cuts erode gains.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Moving profitability goalposts at model labs threaten the demand base for GPU capex.
insights.quote: Anthropic raised its 2026 revenue forecast but pushed back the date it expects to turn cash-flow positive.

insights.claim: Physical limits on land near substations, grid power and patient capital constrain AI build-outs; Microsoft's CFO said expected third-party capacity arrived late.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Power and site scarcity are binding constraints on AI capacity timing.
insights.locator: Two forces are now working against

insights.claim: Power shortages may prevent a CLEC-style glut, but they stretch the time between spending and earning it back, and that gap is where bubbles burst.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Delayed payback, not overcapacity, may be the AI cycle's failure mode.
insights.quote: that gap is where bubbles burst
insights.locator: Two forces are now working against

insights.claim: ChatGPT arrived in November 2022, almost exactly four years before the Nasdaq's October 2026 high, matching the span between the 1996 Telecom Act and the March 2000 peak, suggesting the clock may already be running out.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Implies the author sees the October 2026 Nasdaq high as a possible cycle top.
insights.quote: If the pattern holds, the clock is already running.

insights.claim: A blockbuster Anthropic IPO would complete rather than break the bubble pattern, echoing Palm's March 2, 2000 IPO, briefly worth more than parent 3Com, eight days before the Nasdaq peaked.
insights.speaker: Jonah McLeod
insights.so_what: Treat a euphoric marquee AI IPO as a potential top signal, not a confirmation.
insights.quote: a blockbuster Anthropic debut wouldn’t break the pattern. It would complete it.
